requirements.requirement: The system must ingest raw prescribing data files (e.g., CSV/JSON) and persist them in a staging area without data loss.
The system must validate incoming data against the schema defined in EVAL-P-RX-S1 before processing.
The system must normalize drug identifiers (e.g., NDC, brand/generic names) into a canonical drug representation.
The system must aggregate prescription records by provider using NPI as the primary key.
The system must map normalized drug records to ICD-10 conditions using the icd10_loader taxonomy when a deterministic mapping exists.
The system must persist normalized and aggregated provider-level prescription data in a queryable datastore.
The system must log ingestion job status, including success, partial success, and failure states.
The system must reject and log records that fail schema validation without stopping the entire pipeline.
The system must flag prescriptions that cannot be mapped to any ICD-10 condition for downstream handling.
The system must use an LLM to infer condition mappings for prescriptions lacking deterministic ICD-10 matches.
The system must ensure LLM-generated mappings include a confidence score for each inferred condition.
The system must store both deterministic and LLM-inferred mappings with provenance metadata indicating mapping method.
The system must limit LLM inference to only unmapped prescriptions to avoid overwriting deterministic mappings.
The system must handle LLM inference failures by marking the prescription as unmapped and continuing processing.
The system must process large datasets in batches to prevent memory overflow during ingestion.
The system must ensure idempotent ingestion such that reprocessing the same dataset does not create duplicate records.
